title: Henselian completion rigidity on the open complement
statement:
Let $C$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $I\subseteq C$ be an ideal such that $(C,I)$ is a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Put $\widehat C=\varprojlim_{r\geq1}C/I^r$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], $X=\operatorname{Spec}C$, $\widehat X=\operatorname{Spec}\widehat C$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $U=X\setminus V(I)$, and $\widehat U=\widehat X\times_XU$, where $V(I)$ is the set of primes containing $I$. Let $\pi_U:\widehat U\to U$ be the restriction of the canonical completion morphism. For every torsion abelian sheaf $F$ on the small etale site of $U$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] and every integer $q\geq0$, the canonical inverse-image map is an isomorphism
$$H^q(U_{\mathrm{et}},F)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(\widehat U_{\mathrm{et}},\pi_U^{-1}F).$$
Here inverse image and etale cohomology are [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], and torsion means that each local section is locally killed by a positive integer. There is no excellence, regularity, or constructibility hypothesis. These are the canonical pullback maps, natural in $F$.

source.place: Expose XX section 4.4, printed pp.373--374: abelian comparison to completion (CTC); its Noetherian case is the Fujiwara--Gabber formal base-change theorem, Fujiwara 1995 Corollary 6.6.4. The present cohomology formulation is its open-complement form; in the strictly local case used by the item it is exactly the displayed assertion (*) on p.373.

proof.text: Since $C$ is Noetherian, $I$ is finitely generated. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal], $\widehat C$ is $I\widehat C$-adically complete and $\widehat C/I\widehat C\cong C/I$, compatibly with the quotient maps. By [lem-weil-pbc-complete-pair-henselian], $(\widehat C,I\widehat C)$ is henselian. Thus both pairs needed in the completion argument are henselian. Also $\pi^{-1}(V(I))=V(I\widehat C)$: a prime of $\widehat C$ contains the image of every element of $I$ exactly when its contraction contains $I$. Therefore the open $U'$ in the cited modification results is exactly the stated $\widehat U$, with its stated map $\pi_U$.

source.place: Tag 0ALJ, lemma-complete-henselian, lines 2482--2499; completion algebra from algebra.tex Tag 05GG, lemma-hathat-finitely-generated, lines 22645--22680, as stated in lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-per-admissible-modification-cohomology-presentation] to $(C,I)$ and $F$. It gives the common closed-fibre limit topos $\mathcal T$, coefficient sheaves $L_F^b,L_{\pi_U^{-1}F}^b$, their exchange maps, and a morphism of first-quadrant spectral sequences
$$H^a(\mathcal T,L_F^b)\Longrightarrow H^{a+b}(U,F),\qquad H^a(\mathcal T,L_{\pi_U^{-1}F}^b)\Longrightarrow H^{a+b}(\widehat U,\pi_U^{-1}F).$$
The abutment map is the canonical pullback asked for, not an unspecified comparison. In particular all its maps are natural in $F$.

source.place: XX 4.4, p.373, (**) and its limit; p.374 final Note.

proof.text: Fix a geometric point in the conservative family of [lem-per-admissible-modification-valuative-stalks]. That statement identifies the stalk of $L_F^b\to L_{\pi_U^{-1}F}^b$ with pullback on $H^b$ for a dense inclusion $K_t\hookrightarrow K'_t$ of henselian valued fields and a torsion sheaf $G_t$. These are exactly the hypotheses of [lem-per-dense-henselian-field-etale-comparison], so the stalk map is an isomorphism, for every $b\geq0$. Conservativity of the stated family makes each exchange map of coefficient sheaves an isomorphism. Applying $H^a(\mathcal T,-)$, a functor and hence preserving isomorphisms, proves that every map on the $E_2$ pages of Step 2 is an isomorphism.

source.place: XX 4.4, pp.373--374, valuative-stalk reduction and dense-field Galois comparison.

proof.text: An isomorphism on a spectral-sequence page gives an isomorphism on the next: its inverse commutes with differentials, hence induces inverse maps on their kernels modulo images. Induct on the page. In a fixed bidegree $(a,b)$ of these first-quadrant sequences, for $r>\max(a,b+1)$ both possible differentials to and from that bidegree have a negative coordinate, so are zero. Thus the maps on $E_\infty$ are isomorphisms. For total degree $q$ the filtrations given in Step 2 have only the graded pieces indexed by $0\leq a\leq q$. Starting with their zero terminal terms, induction on this finite filtration proves the abutment map bijective: in each short exact sequence of successive filtration terms, injectivity follows by first mapping to the graded quotient and then to the subterm; surjectivity follows by lifting in the quotient and correcting the lift in the subterm. Therefore the specified pullback on $H^q$ is an isomorphism. This argument applies for $q=0$ too. If $I$ is nilpotent (including $I=0$), both open complements are empty and all the groups in the assertion are zero, so the assertion also holds directly in this degenerate case.
